# dsh-plug-store
English | 中文

A plugin marketplace **inside** DeepSeek Harness. It renders the
dsh-store catalog as a section of t

he host's
Settings page and performs **real** install / update / uninstall / backup by driving the
`
dsh plugin` CLI — not "copy this command" placeholders.

29,593 community plugins in the catalog, 14,344 of them one-click ready, Chinese-first
descriptions,
live progress on every operation, and a task log that survives a restart.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> **npm currently publishes 0.1.21.** The GitHub source is always current and carries
> the last fiv
e fixes; prefer the `github:` form above until the npm release catches up.

Restart the host afterwards, or let profile HMR pick it up: the plugin declares a bundle, so
`dsh.bu
ndle.patch` usually reloads it without a restart.

- **DSH Desktop**: install through the app's own plugin manager. Running the CLI with
`--profile web

` on a desktop machine writes into `profiles/web`, which the Desktop app does not
load — the entry w

ill simply never appear.
- **Which profile it acts on** is resolved in this order: `profile` in the

plugin config → the
directory the plugin itself is installed in (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/…`) → `D

SH_PROFILE` →
`web`. Installing into `desktop` therefore operates on `desktop`.

**Requires a cordis-based DSH host** (developed and verified against 0.2.1-rc.2; peer
`@deepseek-ai/
cordis ^4.0.1`). On an unsupported host the section does not mount.
## Where it shows up

**Settings → Plugin Store** (设置页 → 插件商店), registered through the host's
`settings.section` slot. The

UI is also served at `/dsh-store/` on the host's loopback port, so
you can open it directly in a br

also served at `/dsh-store/` on the host's loopback port, so
you can open it directly in a browser.
## What you get

- **Real installs, not command snippets** — every action shells out to `dsh plugin` against the
corr

ect profile and reports what actually happened. `pnpm` answers "Already up to date" with
exit code 0

when asked to re-add a pinned dependency, so an update explicitly carries the target
version and th

en re-reads what is installed: the UI says *updated* only when a version really
moved, and says *not

hing changed* when it did not.
- **Live progress and a task log** — operations run as queued tasks f

ed by pnpm's `ndjson`
reporter (resolving / downloading / linking / building, current package, byte

counts). Failures
are mapped from 13 `ERR_PNPM_*` codes to plain-language hints. The log persists to

`~/.dsh/store-data/tasks.json`, survives a restart (interrupted tasks are reported as
interrupted r

ather than silently disappearing), and completed or failed rows can be cleared in
one click.
- **"Up

datable" is computed against your machine** — installed version versus the catalog target,
not a fla

g in the data. Locally linked and other non-registry dependencies (`file:`, `link:`,
`workspace:`, `

git+…`) are excluded, so they are never offered an update that would overwrite
them.
- **Chinese-fir

st catalog** — descriptions prefer Chinese; entries that exist only in English are
machine-translate

d at build time (99% of the shipped catalog), and anything still missing is
translated in page on de

mand. The 中 / EN toggle appears only when two genuine languages exist.
- **Themes as a preview wall*

* — theme cards show real screenshots extracted from each repository
README (relative paths resolved

against `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `blob` links rewritten),
landscape shots only, click for a lig

htbox with prev/next.
- **Browsing that scales** — real pagination (24/48/96 per page, remembered),

17 bilingual
categories, search across name / description / tags, filters (installable / official /

new this
week / updatable / favorites / installed), seven sort orders including random, card and lis

t
views, collapsible "recently added" and "most installed" rails, and a bottom queue bar that
batche

s installs into one confirmed run.
[该节后续省略]
## Data

The catalog is built daily by
`qianyumeng0228/dsh-store` and published to GitHub
Pages. This plugin

reads it through its own same-origin route (`/dsh-store/data/plugins.json`),
which caches the snapsh

ot at `~/.dsh/store-data/plugins.json` for 24 hours and refreshes in the
background once stale — ope

ning the store stays fast and does not depend on the CDN being
reachable at that moment. Responses a
re gzip-negotiated with a weak ETag.

The snapshot is deliberately **not** vendored into the package: shipping it would freeze a copy
that
goes stale daily, and the cache above already gives the same first-paint speed.
## Host API
All routes live under `/dsh-store/`; the `api/*` ones are guarded (see Security).
| Route | Purpose |

| `GET /api/capabilities` | feature discovery; the UI switches into host mode on seeing it |
| `GET

/api/installed` | installed package names, versions, kinds and source repos |
| `POST /api/install`

| `{source:"npm",name,version?}` or `{source:"github",repo,ref?}` → `202 {taskId}` |
| `POST /api/up

date` | same payload; returns `from` / `to` / `changed` |
| `POST /api/uninstall` | real removal, tw

o-step confirmation in the UI |
| `GET /api/tasks` | queued, running and finished tasks with progres

s |
| `POST /api/tasks/clear` | drop completed and failed rows only |
[该节后续省略]
## Security

- API routes require a **loopback `Host`** (`localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`) **plus** a custom
`

x-dsh-store: 1` header — a cross-site page cannot set that header without a preflight it will
lose.

The page itself and the catalog stay open, because they are public data.
- **Zero runtime dependenci

es**, and no telemetry: the only outbound request is the catalog fetch.
- The plugin reads no creden

tials. It writes only inside `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/` (through
`dsh plugin`) and `~/.dsh/store-d

ata/` (its own task log and data cache).
- Install sources are limited to catalog entries; the store

does not accept an arbitrary URL as a
plugin source.
- Plugins from git sources may need build-scri

pt approval (`allowBuilds`) in the host; the queue
surfaces that instead of hiding it.
- Listing is
not endorsement. Every entry is third-party code — install what you trust.
